source.title: Claims: Abhinavagupta argues the two-aspect structure is self-ground
source.author: Codex/Hermes loop

source_span.quote: TĀ 4/9: consciousness is by its very nature full (nirbharā), with nothing to sub

claims.claim_text: TĀ 4/9: consciousness is by its very nature full (nirbharā), with nothing to subtract or add. There is nothing separate from it on which it depends. The two-aspect structure does not require an external ground — it is self-grounding through the Heart (vimarśa) which is the foundation (pratiṣṭhā) of consciousness itself.
claims.hetu: consciousness is svātmasaṃvitti, full in itself, depending on nothing
claims.sadhya: the two-aspect structure is self-grounding through vimarśa, not through a separate prior consciousness
claims.vyapti_statement: If consciousness needs nothing outside itself and its foundation is the Heart, then the ground is internal to the structure.

falsifier.condition: Show that Abhinavagupta posits Anuttara as a genuinely separate ontological ground beyond the two-aspect structure, not as the same reality under a different aspect.
